key_insight: Conditional Flow Matching can generate realistic 3D instantaneous urban wind and temperature fields from building geometry and mean flow, capturing turbulence variability that deterministic surrogates miss.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, LES-like microclimate prediction for urban design and climate adaptation workflows where repeated high-fidelity simulation would be too costly.
method: Generative CFM model conditioned on geometry and mean-flow inputs
Shared-noise initialization to preserve spatial continuity and reduce GPU memory demand
evidence_signal: Compared with LES, the surrogate achieved low NRMSE for first-order statistics (2.99% wind, 1.77% temperature) and strong agreement on second-order turbulence metrics, TKE, PDFs, and vertical profiles.
watch_item: Because generation is still data-driven and relies on overlapping subdomain stitching, robustness to unseen urban morphologies and very large domains should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Conditional Flow Matching for Generation of 3D Multi-variable Instantaneous Urban Microclimate Fields
